indicators.note: being on board a vessel means sitting inside it, so one piece goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the crossword's usual vessel to be on board
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Pacing the deck of a ship to discover where the cabins are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the classic signal to go inside SS, steamship. 'Rooms' is not chambers but free places, as in room for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms in the sense of free capacity or available places, as in 'there is room for two more'.

clue.text: Referee's rubbish skill one supporter elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
an art is a skill
Roman numeral one
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A referee's poor technique, held up by a single fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay; ROT+ART+I+BRA is then written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are impartial people appointed to settle a dispute and make a binding judgement, so they are synonyms.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of bear, put up with
second meaning: the dull talker who corners you at the bar

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the pub is just colour: the second meaning is the dull person, wherever found.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb bear matches a word for someone who wearies listeners with dull talk.

clue.text: One's climbing taking a distant expedition

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside
in a down clue, climbing means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: one is I, plus the 's read as 'is' gives I and S
A, plus far for distant

explanation.surface: A mountaineer embarking on a far-off journey.
explanation.walkthrough: I'S goes up to become SI, which then takes A FAR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland journey or hunting trip, especially in East Africa, so it is a kind of expedition.

clue.text: Reports a government's leader in failures

indicators.note: placing things in something puts them inside it

parts.note: messes are botched efforts, failures
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of government

explanation.surface: News stories about a premier caught up in a series of fiascos.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus G sits inside MESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports in the sense of communicated pieces of information sent from one party to another.

clue.text: Badgering male animal protecting animal males

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a hart is a male deer
a donkey
men are males

explanation.surface: A stag harrying while guarding a group of male beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badgering' tempts you to look for a badger in the animal theme, but it is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgering used as a noun means persistent pestering, which is what harassment is: an exact synonym.

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the first letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: JD Vance waiting for the top job to come his way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: JD Vance, US vice-president, hoping one day to be president.
explanation.definitionFit: Veep is American slang for a vice-president, the office Vance holds while expecting to rise higher.

clue.text: Viciousness or callousness holding up game

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top
the words hold the run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Brutality or cruelty that delays a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through viciousnESS OR CALlousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Punch from goalkeeper for a team

indicators.note: taking letters from the words that follow, rather than from their meaning

parts.note: the run of letters starting near the end of the first word

explanation.surface: A keeper punching the ball clear on behalf of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: goalkeePER FOR A TEam. 'Punch' looks like a goalkeeper's save, but here it is the verb to make a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To punch a hole through paper or metal is to pierce it, which is what perforate means.

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for new
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction: bowl a new spell because the last over has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' and 'over' make it sound like cricket, but bowl is the definition and over reverses A N ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a stadium shaped like a bowl, such as the Rose Bowl, so an arena by another name.

indicators.note: placed after, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: to ring a bell is to chime

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens only now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Fantasy dreams following Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Ring suggests Wagner or Tolkien, but it is just the verb for a bell sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an impossible illusion or wild imagining, named after a mythical monster, so a fantasy.

clue.text: One under canvas on second frolic

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means set after, so pieces join in sequence

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
someone sleeping in a tent is a camper

explanation.surface: A tent-dweller playing about for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' is the idiom for sleeping in a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run about playfully, which is a way to romp or frolic: synonyms as verbs.

indicators.note: the back letter is moved to the front, rotating the word by one

parts.note: trappings are accessories or ornaments

explanation.surface: Sturdy add-ons, worn the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' here is not a full reversal: only the last letter, the S, moves to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapping person is big, healthy and robust, so the adjective is a synonym for strong.

parts.note: a prop is a support
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen
level scores are even, or tied

explanation.surface: Backing the monarch even though she holds estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' reads as 'even though', but it means level, as in a tied match.
explanation.definitionFit: The propertied classes are those who own real estate, so the adjective means holding land.

indicators.note: a mask covers, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: spots as a verb, notices, sees
M is the abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: A spotty complexion hiding a man's good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Spots and looks both read as nouns, but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Looks as in 'it looks likely', meaning appears, so a synonym for this verb.

parts.note: to infiltrate is to enter covertly
to prise is to force open

explanation.surface: A covert police unit getting inside and showing some go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a noun, a police force, but it is the verb to lever open.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise means readiness to take bold action and resourcefulness, which is what initiative is.

clue.text: Sailor withdrawing chains losing right tack

indicators.note: to withdraw is to pull back, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: losing something means it drops out

parts.note: irons are chains or fetters
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sailor unclamping fetters while abandoning the correct course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack' in a sailing surface wants to be a change of course; it is food, as in hardtack, the ship's biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is an old word for food or provisions, so it matches the allotted provisions issued to sailors or soldiers.

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule, government
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A cabinet reshuffle moving a clown in the ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: Government here is the period of rule, not the ministers; the question mark admits the cheeky view of politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign someone is to move them to a new post or task, which is what transfer means as a verb.

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: US for American
spends as a noun, sums paid out

explanation.surface: Police detaining a Yank over money handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrests' reads as police seizures; it is the verb to halt, as in arresting progress.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a process is to stop or halt it, which is to suspend it: verb synonyms in the sense of halting.

clue.text: Spirit of honour about to end

indicators.note: the word's opening 'about' is sent to the end, rotating the letters

parts.note: to honour someone is to respect them

explanation.surface: A sense of honour about to expire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to end' reads as 'nearly over', but RE, a crossword word for about, is what moves from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or apparition, which is a spirit in the supernatural sense.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Admitting that something is very nearly sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: Almost GREED loses its D after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, which is the plain meaning of agree: verb synonyms.

clue.text: Covered empty loft before in outhouse

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the outer letters
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Something stored first in the attic and then in the garden shed, kept out of the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: An outhouse is a small outbuilding, and ERE is poetic for before, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in the sense of protected from weather or danger, which is what a sheltered spot is.

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way

parts.note: the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter
the S of the possessive, taken as written
livid can mean ashen or pallid, so pale

explanation.surface: A lover furious about a come-on.
explanation.walkthrough: Livid usually means furious, but its older sense is ghostly pale. Note 'Sweetheart' must be split.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse or pass as it goes by: verb synonyms describing time slipping away.

clue.text: Suggest supporting Democrat having cheeky features?

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support is to sit underneath, so this piece comes second

parts.note: D for Democrat
to imply is to suggest

explanation.surface: Hinting that you back a Democrat who has an impudent streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' suggests impudence; the question mark flags it as literally of the cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimples are small hollows in the cheeks, so a face marked with them has features on the cheek.

clue.text: Cover the woman with adult article

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the pieces are joined together

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
the definite article

explanation.surface: A magazine cover featuring a woman alongside a grown-up story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like a noun, a magazine front page, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to encase in a protective covering, like a sword in its scabbard: a verb synonym.

parts.note: E for European
a dam is an animal's mother; a cow can be one

explanation.surface: Cheese made from the milk of a continental cow.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a cow is only one example of a dam, a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch cheese with a red wax rind, and cheese is made from milk on the farm.

clue.text: Sheet could be one of these

definitions.text: Sheet could be one of these

parts.words: Sheet could be one of these
parts.note: surface reading: a bed sheet or sheet of paper might be one of some set of items
setter's reading: the word 'sheet' is a rearrangement of the letters of the last word of the clue

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: shuffle THESE and you get SHEET, so 'sheet' is one of the word puzzles in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging all the letters of another is the device this whole clue names.

parts.note: A for ace, as on playing cards

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means raising, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A brilliant number elevated by a singer's solo performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A then AIR written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is an elaborate song for one voice in an opera or oratorio, so a solo for the voice.

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A golf tournament held to raise money for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Charity here is not a fundraising body but the virtue of goodwill.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace in the religious sense of unearned kindness and love is close to charity as a Christian virtue.

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it around you, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them
S is the abbreviation for small
a miss is an error or failed attempt

explanation.surface: Spotting a tiny flaw on someone wearing a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' reads as the verb to spot; it is the noun, as in being given your notice at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given notice means being told your job is ending, which is a firing or sacking from employment.
